regrade.instruction: Orchestrator obligation 1: re-grade all 43 external findings where codex said S1 and the register said S2, S3 or S4, reading the code at the audit base first and accepting neither side.

entries.reason: The public buy passes only value, so ethers uses market fees and a node gas estimate with no cap. It runs only on the operator-invoked deliberate path (snipes stay private at bot.ts:1431) and spends one transaction of market gas behind the affordability re-check, so the capital effect is bounded: S2, not S1.

Quoting the threshold as an exact input proves nothing about depth: an exact-input quote on a thin V3 pool fills what it can and does not revert, so every V3 pool with any active liquidity passes the minimum-liquidity gate on an ordinary condition. The register's stated bound does not hold (minOut comes from the same thin-pool quote and the honeypot roundtrip measures tax against the quote at trade size), so a capital risk limit is bypassed: S1.

The V2 check hardcodes 1 native, which equals the BSC default and is stricter than the ETH, Base and Arbitrum defaults (0.5, 0.1, 0.1), so at defaults it refuses more, never less; only a chain configured above 1 native is under-enforced (S3 on its own). The entry's grade is S1 from codex-BUY-12.

checkHoneypot has no caller at the base (git grep for checkHoneypot( matches only its definition; bot.ts:8 only imports it), so the key-in-error path cannot run today and codex's S1 needs a caller that does not exist. Held at S2, not S3, because a single added call would put the private key in a warn log.

The catch at :1585-1588 also handles a single RPC error from decodeReceipt (receiptDecoder.ts:44 has no try) or a SQLite error, so no crash is needed and the register's condition was too narrow; rationale corrected. The repeat sale still executes at market for tokens the wallet holds and the proceeds return to the wallet, so it over-liquidates a position above its tier rather than losing principal: S2.

The 1000-raw-unit floor only matters for a whole position below 1000 raw units, which needs a 0 to 2 decimal token and a failed sale; 9 and 18 decimal launches get a negligible floor. A rare token shape, so S3 stands.

EXIT_DUST_THRESHOLD_BPS has no upper bound, so 10000 tears down a held position after a failed sale, but it needs an operator to set an out-of-range value (default 1 = 0.01%). Misconfiguration-only with a sane default: S2.

Approvals and the public fallback carry no fee or gas override, but each pays market gas for one transaction and the private leg still applies its ceiling; no configured cap is exceeded by more than one transaction of market gas. S2 stands.

Teardown does trust latest-state balance at one confirmation, as codex says. A reorg that removes a mined sell and does not re-mine it is rare on these four chains, so S3 stands (AUD-TX-012 is the transaction-layer twin).

Teardown does not cancel queued work, but isTokenSniped blocks re-entry into a token already traded, so stale work finds zero balance and cleans up; the only path around it is the double-buy race already escalated as AUD-BUY-004. S3 stands.
Approvals do not reset to zero first, so a zero-first token with a leftover nonzero allowance reverts the approve. Both conditions together are uncommon for new launches; S3 stands.

Codex's claim cannot happen: slippagePercent is the literal 5 at config.ts:282 (not an env value), so the || 5 fallback never fires. The entry's actual concern (quoting before an approve with no timeout) is unaffected and stays S2.

Completed tiers are stored as array indices and re-read against a re-parsed sorted list, so inserting a tier while positions are open repeats a sale. It needs an operator to change PARTIAL_SELL_TARGETS across a restart and the repeat is a sale at market above the tier: S2.

Private V2 partials use swapExactTokensForETH, so a taxed token reverts and partial take-profit never fires, as codex says. All three strategies simulate before sending, so the retries burn no gas, and the position keeps its routine exits and the FoT public fallback; the effect is bounded: S2.

Signal 3 divides raw WETH out by raw tokens in, so for 18-decimal tokens priced below 0.5 WETH it always trips (the signal is inert) and for few-decimal tokens it rarely trips, leaving signals 1 and 2 to decide V3 exits; a complete liquidity pull still trips through the quoter revert at :1766-1775. The result is a wrongful or missed V3 emergency exit on one position, bounded: S2.

HTTP polling requests the whole outstanding range and keeps lastBlock on failure, so a gap above the provider limit never clears; it applies only to chains with no WebSocket URL and the routine exit monitor runs independently. One protection layer lost, not every exit: S2.

Each HTTP-mode registration adds another never-stopped poller, so a rug log is dispatched N times; the sell lock still serializes the sells. The consequence that can hurt money (breaker over-count) is carried at S1 by AUD-ANTIRUG-003, so this entry stays S2.
Same entry: with no in-flight guard a slow tick can re-dispatch a range and move the cursor back. The sell lock prevents a double sell; breaker over-counting is AUD-ANTIRUG-003 at S1. S2 stands.

pendingV3Burn is keyed by pool only, so a second position on the same pool replaces the first watcher; that needs two positions on one pool (the AUD-BUY-004 double buy) and the Collect path still evaluates each. S3 stands.

Any Collect consumes the pending Burn, as codex says, but the withdrawn funds only leave on a Collect that is then evaluated with its own owner, so an unrelated allowlisted Collect delays evaluation rather than skipping the real one. S3 stands.
Repeated Burns do restart the five-block grace with no limit, as codex says, but the withdrawal needs a Collect, which is evaluated when it arrives. Delay only: S3.

Codex's crash path needs an alert to reject, but sendCtxAlert catches Telegram errors (notifier.ts:80-88) and broadcast skips closed sockets, so the reconnect loop survives. The entry's actual concern (signals report connected while no subscription exists) stays S2.

ethers v6 on() builds the subscription with no network call and starts it without awaiting, so a discarded on() promise does not reject on an RPC or socket failure; only an invalid filter would, and the filter here is hex addresses. S3 stands; the process-crash class is AUD-TX-009 and AUD-ANTIRUG-002.

The gate ignores removed logs but re-evaluates live pool state at confirm time, so a reorged-out withdrawal can only sell if the pool still trips all three signals then. No capital effect was found beyond a false positive that needs a reorg: S3.

The breaker is memory-only, as codex says, so a restart clears a trip and up to the threshold of further anti-rug sells can run before it trips again. It needs a restart during a misfiring detector and each sell is one position: S2.

LP Transfer logs use their own recipient, so an allowlisted withdrawal through the router can trip the pair and zero-address transfer evaluations, but only for allowlisted LP flows and as a false-positive sale at market. S3 stands.

The cast would fail only for number or string gas and value, but every builder passes bigint (maxGasLimit is bigint, buy value is parseEther output at bot.ts:1044 and :1359). No caller reaches the failing case: S4.

Buy builders go through wallet.populateTransaction and sell builders set only gasLimit, and each strategy overrides the fee fields from its own feeData snapshot; a mismatch needs the RPC fee model to change between the two calls, so it is unreachable in practice: S4 (rationale corrected).

Bids can repeat when the market priority exceeds the escalation step and can miss a node replacement bump, so a retry may be refused, as codex says. Sells then fall through to the public fallback and buys fail clean, so this delays rather than loses: S2.

BundleIncluded returns success with no status check, as codex says, but the exit path re-reads balanceOf before teardown, so a status-0 sell is caught and the position stays monitored; codex's close-without-selling outcome is not reachable on the sell path. The remaining effect is a mis-recorded buy: S3.

A first-block receipt is accepted with no reorg handling, as codex says, but a reorg deep enough to drop a mined transaction is rare on these chains and a dropped transaction usually re-lands. S3 stands.

Confirmed: the strategies call buildReconcileConfig with no leg, so sells use the buy priority ceiling. The defaults are equal (25 gwei both) and the affordability clamp still bounds spend, so the effect is a non-default ceiling that does nothing: S2.

The reserve omits priority and Base L1 data fees, as codex says, but the entry gate also adds the per-chain fixed cushion and sizing uses maxGasLimit (several times a real sell), so only a wallet funded to the floor is short. S3 stands.

No code path checks an absolute gas price (no such guard exists in src), as codex says. The bid is base fee plus the clamped priority, so a spike costs market gas for one transaction at a time and no configured ceiling is exceeded: S2.

A failed relay call logs the whole axios error, so the Authorization header and a signed transaction can reach local logs, as codex says. It moves no funds and needs log access: S2, same grade as the sibling credential leaks.
A negative per-chain buffer is accepted and lowers both floors, as codex says, but only an operator setting a negative number reaches it (the template defaults are positive). S3 stands.
Multipliers below 1 pass parseExitGateBuffer (finite and above 0), so 0.1 underfunds the reserve, but it needs a non-default operator value. S3 stands, as DB-04.

parseFloat turns a non-numeric TRAILING value into NaN and disables that trailing check, as codex says, but it needs a non-numeric typo with sane defaults and parseFloat tolerates forms like 15%. Misconfiguration-only: S2.

The v3 rebuild is not transactional and a crash mid-way would leave a half-migrated file, as codex says, but it is one historical step, later steps are transactional, and the bot refuses to boot rather than trade on a bad schema. S3 stands.

WAL with synchronous=NORMAL can lose the last commits on power loss or an OS crash, as codex says, but not on a process crash, and only within the OS write-back window after a write. A real but narrow condition with no battery guarantee: S2.
A failed parse of a legacy .bot-state.json only logs and continues, but the path needs a pre-Phase-4 file next to an empty database, which no current install has. Legacy path: S4.
Legacy-imported rows have NULL amount_in and count as zero exposure, as codex says, but this needs the same stale state file next to an empty database. S3 stands.

Every failed Telegram call logs the whole axios error, which carries the request URL and bot token, as codex says. That needs log access and the token does not move funds (only the notifier uses it): S2.
